jurisdiction.name: Ethiopia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ethiopia governs AI mainly by setting up institutions: the Artificial Intelligence Institute, established by Council of Ministers Regulation 510/2022 and accountable to the Prime Minister, is charged with drafting national AI policy and law, and a 2026 regulation created the Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence. The 2024 Personal Data Protection Proclamation gives a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, including profiling, with the Ethiopian Communications Authority as regulator. A National AI Policy reportedly approved in June 2024 and the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy, which tasks the AI Institute with a national AI strategy and an AI ethics framework, have no official full texts online.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The National AI Policy and Digital Ethiopia 2030 could not be found as official texts and are listed as leads. As a large country with few records, Ethiopia is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Institute Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation No. 510/2022
instruments.current_status: In force since publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (28th Year No. 32) on 23 April 2022 (Art. 16). Issued bilingually in Amharic and English; the Ministry of Justice portal title wrongly adds 'Customs Regulation' to the English title. Regulation No. 588/2026 makes the Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence accountable to the Institute.
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers regulation (issued under Proclamation No. 1263/2021) establishing the Artificial Intelligence Institute as an autonomous federal institution accountable to the Prime Minister, with objectives of AI research, development and deployment, setting enabling national AI policy and infrastructure frameworks, and building an AI startup ecosystem. Its powers include formulating, drafting and monitoring national AI policies, laws and regulatory frameworks, and supporting national security decision-making with AI. It transfers the rights and obligations of the AI Research and Development Center to the Institute and repeals Artificial Intelligence Center Regulation No. 463/2020.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Ethiopia's national AI body, which is mandated to draft national AI policy and regulation.

instruments.current_status: In force from publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (30th Year No. 35) on 24 July 2024 (Art. 70). Implementing directives of the Ethiopian Communications Authority were not located on official sites (see leads).
instruments.summary: Ethiopia's first comprehensive personal data protection law, applying to processing by automated and non-automated means and designating the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulatory authority. Article 31 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, plus rights to human intervention and to express their views, with exceptions for contracts, laws with safeguards and explicit consent; automated evaluation of personal aspects may not be based on sensitive data. Controllers must disclose the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and its envisaged effects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law with explicit automated-decision and profiling rules that govern AI systems processing personal data.

instruments.current_status: In force from publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (32nd Year No. 19) on 17 March 2026 (Art. 6). The Ministry of Justice portal lists it twice (a second Amharic-titled entry for the same regulation).
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers regulation, issued under the university autonomy Proclamation No. 1294/2023, establishing the Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence as an autonomous university with its main campus in Addis Ababa. Notwithstanding the general university regime, the University is accountable to the Artificial Intelligence Institute, and the Ministry of Education's powers over it are delegated to its board, which may issue implementing directives.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Extends the national AI institutional set-up: a public AI university placed under the Artificial Intelligence Institute.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. Laws read via the Ministry of Justice portal (justice.gov.et, mirrors the Federal Negarit Gazeta) in English and Amharic. mint.gov.et reset; aii.et script-rendered with no listings; pmo.gov.et Digital Ethiopia 2030 PDF returned the app shell/503 (only a draft copy on the National Bank site, kept as a lead under the third-party-host rule). Standards and procurement agencies not searched. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Ministry of Justice federal law portal (justice.gov.et, mirrors Federal Negarit Gazette) searched in English and Amharic: Regulation 510/2022 (AI Institute), Regulation 588/2026 (Medemer AI University) and Proclamation 1321/2024 (data protection, Art. 31 automated decisions) found and read. Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Proclamation 1426/2026 and Startup Proclamation 1396/2024 (general regulatory sandbox) checked: no AI-specific provisions. No AI bill, deepfake offence or public-sector algorithm rule found.; Government: National AI Policy (2024): no official text online (lead). Digital Ethiopia 2030: official PMO PDF not retrievable, draft read via a central-bank-hosted copy (lead). aii.et and pmo.gov.et are client-side apps with no retrievable document listings; mint.gov.et reset connections.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no ministry-level AI strategy, guidance or playbook (education, health, justice, finance, labour) located on official sites; Ministry of Education's link is the Medemer AI University regulation.; Regulators: Ethiopian Communications Authority (data protection regulator): eca.et resources/directives page checked, lists only the Proclamation 1321/2024 itself, no PDP directives or AI guidance. INSA: no AI security guidance found. National Bank of Ethiopia: no AI directive found. Searched, nothing found for standards, procurement, transparency, sandbox (AI-specific), generative AI, index-readiness.. Not reached: mint.gov.et (connection reset); aii.et document pages (client-side app, no listings); Ethiopian Standards Agency (ISO/IEC 42001 adoption) not searched; Public Procurement and Property Authority not searched. Could not verify: National AI Policy (2024) text and adoption date (no official copy); Digital Ethiopia 2030 final text and adoption date (pmo.gov.et PDF not served); Regulation 463/2020 gazette text. strategy, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.note: Reported approved by the Council of Ministers at its 37th regular session (27 June 2024) and cited in the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy as 'The AI Policy (2024)'. No official full text found on aii.et (site is a client-side app with no listed documents), mint.gov.et (connection reset) or justice.gov.et; the only online copies are on non-official hosts. Promote once an official copy is published.

leads.title: Digital Ethiopia 2030
leads.issuing_authority: Federal Government of Ethiopia (Office of the Prime Minister; Ministry of Innovation and Technology)
leads.note: Official PDF at https://www.pmo.gov.et/media/other/Digital_Ethiopia_2030.pdf (curl returned only the site's app shell; WebFetch HTTP 503). A copy labelled 'Draft' is hosted by the National Bank of Ethiopia (nbe.gov.et/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Draft_Digital_Ethiopia_2030.pdf, read in full): it integrates the National AI Policy (2024), names AI among enabling technologies, and tasks the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute with leading a National AI Strategy and overseeing an AI Innovation and Ethics Framework. No publication or adoption date stated in the document; reportedly approved by the Council of Ministers in late 2025. Record once the PMO/MInT copy and an official date are confirmed. It succeeds Digital Ethiopia 2025.
